sentences.text: A magnet can pull on some metals, but not on every metal.
Iron, nickel, and cobalt are metals a magnet can attract.
Wood, plastic, cloth, and aluminum do not stick to an ordinary magnet.
A steel paper clip sticks because steel has iron in it.
Every magnet has two ends, called the north pole and the south pole.
Opposite poles pull toward each other.
Two north poles, or two south poles, push apart.
You can feel that push if you try to press those matching ends together.
Magnets are useful in compasses, in many toys, and inside some spinning motors.

questions.prompt: What is this passage mostly about?

choices.text: How to build a motor from wood
Why aluminum is a kind of cloth
How paper clips are made in a factory
Which things magnets pull, and how their poles act

questions.explanation: The passage lists metals a magnet can pull, materials it cannot pull, and how the two poles attract or push. Those ideas cover the whole passage.

questions.prompt: Which of these sticks to an ordinary magnet?
questions.explanation: The passage says a steel paper clip sticks because steel has iron in it. It also says aluminum, wood, and plastic do not stick.

questions.prompt: In this passage, attract means what?
questions.explanation: The passage says a magnet can attract iron, nickel, and cobalt, right after saying a magnet can pull on some metals. Attract means to pull toward.
